[h1]创意内容均不容小觑的DRPG优秀之作[/h1] [h2]游戏推荐指数：★★★★★★★★★☆[/h2] [quote]买肯定是要买的，玩肯定是不玩的 快来关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/38222893/] G胖受害者鉴赏家[/url] 让选择游戏变得更加简单[/quote] 令人感到十分惊艳的游戏设计，同时游戏内容和深度也相当丰富，既有传统的地下城要素，也有不少新创新，把第一人称自由探索和回合制战斗结合的相当有趣，同时还加入距离和小队玩法要素给整个游玩过程带来了相当愉快的体验。 游戏的玩法为DRPG，玩家在地下城内采用第一人称自由移动，每次只能进行90°转向不存在斜向的情况，同时玩家虽然是自由移动但是游戏却在对战中加入了距离内容，根据玩家发起/触发战斗时玩家距离敌方的距离进行整数划分来判定玩家与敌方距离，这种第一人称自由移动＋回合制战斗的玩法初见还是相当惊艳的。 人物立绘和人物职业玩家可以自由搭配，属性上游戏共给予了5个维度，同时设置了可供玩家选择的主属性与副属性来作为人物升级后的属性提升内容，职业上游戏供给予了超过5个职业，每种职业各有特色，技能也不同每个职业的技能还是相当多的，除去职业技能外还有公共技能，所有职业均可学习。 装备方面，游戏设置了三种装备内容，饰品/防具/武器，每种装备内容都较为充实，并且不同装备有相符较好的职业，装备属性和攻击机制也不尽相同，装备不仅可以玩家带入，也可以在地宫中开宝箱开出或者从商人处购买。 地宫中设计了各种不同的可互动内容，商人，宝箱，神秘房间，祭坛等等，各种随机NPC和互动内容很有DND的味道，每个可互动内容给出选择也不少，玩家无法直接判断每个互动内容结果的好坏，带来了较大的随机性，丰富了游玩内容，部分互动内容还需要根据玩家属性/状态进行判定，带来了一些策略元素。 游戏的怪物和技能BUFF相当丰富270种技能＋86种敌方怪物使得玩家在多周目游玩中也不会有特别高的重复感，也是本作ROUGUE LIKE元素的核心，每种怪物差异性较大，并不是简单的换皮，玩家需要仔细小心的制定战斗策略（游戏难度并不低，很容易暴毙）结合怪物种类，角色技能，装备，药物来制定策略。 游戏的美术画面也很有特色有点像《奥博拉丁的回归》和老式《DOOM》的结合，画面相当有特色各种CG过场也不含糊，并且怪物颜色和环境颜色时强对比色，加上游戏暗红色的环境颜色，给游戏带来了一些恐怖氛围，笔者在游玩过程中好几次被突脸怪物吓到。 游戏地图为随机（肉鸽玩法）同时游戏还引入了独特的心神玩法（节省TP强化攻击）并且游戏允许玩家自定义角色（自由度极高）立绘＋职业＋技能＋武器自由搭配，分配点数，多周目体验不同搭配体验很爽，每次都时完全不同的游玩体验。 游戏的缺点是没有教学，基本教学没有给出，熟悉DRPG或者CRPG的玩家可能上手较快，初次之外要是能开放创意工房玩家之间互相分享自己设计的各种人物立绘和武器装备人物角色那么游戏将来的潜力难以想象。 [quote][h3]鉴赏员测评配置：[/h3] CPU：RYZEN 7600X GPU：AMD 7900XTX 加入[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/GgamePlayer] G胖受害者鉴赏组[/url] 和鉴赏员一起战斗！爽！ [/quote]

[h1]地牢探索指北——接下来，屁股蹭墙很有用[/h1] [h2] “偷袭敌人时，敌人盯着你👁👁是正常的” “新生的暗黑魔法师被地牢唾弃” “接下来，屁股蹭墙很有用” [/h2] …… 我在游玩《祭祀地宫》后抱着复杂的心情总结出这些话。相信我，这对一个被打上“困难”标签的游戏是很有用的 先来讲讲新生的暗黑魔法师为什么会被地牢唾弃——这款游戏里怪物对不同属性的攻击有不同抗性，比如我遇到一只腐尸这种典型的死灵生物，直接给它一个光属性的驱邪术给它净化咯——但是，它对暗影属性的魔法就完全免疫了。 可怕的是，第一层几乎全是死灵生物，所以一开始如果你找到的队友只会一个暗属性的恶咒术，那你接下来也要变成死灵生物咯（ps：制作组请优化前期这部分体验） [h2] “你怎么取了屁股蹭墙这个标题？” “你不觉得这标题很神圣吗？” [/h2] 咳咳…实际上和这游戏的机制有关——它是将玩家移动和回合制战斗融合在一起的，也就是说玩家的战斗，也会受到你和怪物之间的距离等影响。 而这又不得不提到另一个机制“心神”了。简单来讲，这就是个节省耗蓝还能强化攻击的buff。不要小瞧了它哦，和我一样掌握它的机制就能实现就算只是遇到一只小怪也可以随便使用最高规格的魔法送走它。 “心神”在非战斗时是依据玩家的移动格数来恢复的，就是你只要走够多就能恢复——但如果你这么走，可能遇到的情况就是走一半还没恢复好就又遇上怪了。 为避免这种情况，我研究出了“屁股蹭墙”——即背靠墙壁，不断后撤就能快速恢复心神（当然，其实反复前进后退和向前撞墙也可以） 那如果遇到怪了呢？别慌！我们可以借助地形来应付它们，比如说像这种拐角，我们就可以利用它后退为恢复“心神”争取更多时间——“后退不是逃跑，而是我要开始蓄力了！“ 那“偷袭敌人时，敌人盯着你是正常的”又怎么回事呢？ 这就不得不提到这游戏里的一个技能了！当我队员学到“处决”这技能时，我犯难了——给敌人上debuff得多用一个技能，那这技能怎么用？ [h2]我直接偷袭不就好了！[/h2] 我直接一个绕后跑到小怪背后…… [h2] “👁👁” [/h2] https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3682264527 [h2]你别这样盯着我，这样影响我偷袭[/h2] 像偷袭这样的操作需要“主动进入战斗”——了解这一小技巧可以给你提供先手优势，譬如还有在敌人离你还远时先远程释放魔法攻击。 像“处决”这样的特别技能还有很多，诶！你怎么知道我用“武艺精通”后打出五百多伤害（快去玩吧，不然我这伤害都不知道和谁说） “武艺精通”——“未装备武器时，伤害随等级提升” 这就涉及如何培养一个角色的问题了！技能，武器，携带遗物等，都能很大程度影响这个角色的强度。 诶！☝🤓开出一个“穿戴视为徒手攻击”的武器！再让他学一个提高技能伤害百分比的技能！数值这不就膨胀起来了！ 目前游玩有个翻译bug——你开箱子收集的物品中文显示错误，不会弹出“你打开宝箱发现了什么”只能打开背包才能看到自己获得了什么 目前游玩有个翻译bug——你开箱子收集的物品中文显示错误，不会弹出“你打开宝箱发现了什么”只能打开背包才能看到自己获得了什么 不得不说的是，我个人游玩下来认为这款游戏难度偏大，但细细游玩下来能发现其深度之大，对回合制地牢探险感兴趣的话可以尝试一下 [h2]快来玩吧 快下地宫吧 地宫还需要更多人 👁👁 👁👁 👁👁[/h2] [h1] 游戏推荐指数：★★★★★★★★☆☆[/h1] [quote=] 买肯定是要买的，玩肯定是不玩的 快来关注 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/38222893/] G胖受害者鉴赏家 [/url] 让选择游戏变得更加简单 [/quote]

Really, really stylish, focused, and doesn't waste your time at all. For under $10 on sale this is a steal. If you're interested, pick it up. It's got imagination for ages and the monsters and level graphics match. It also will outright kill you if you're stupid, so don't be stupid. Dummy.

吹这游戏的我都不知道是什么人，太变态了我只能说 喜欢受虐待还叫爽的我不评价 玩游戏就是要有快乐，不管是享受构筑也好，地牢探险也好，都是要给人正反馈的 看看这个游戏是在干什么：本游戏的核心思想就是随机，是的，纯随机 我是真玩力竭了，初始人物随半天属性好不容易能看了进去了，然后给的野外加入的人物：野蛮人，随了一身法师技能，好么又来个指挥官，一看技能，嘲讽（增加怪打你几率）+隐匿（减少怪打你几率） 然后局内还要看属性随机成长，看随机掉落（运气好进去给你掉几件特效145防具+70特效武器，运气差40的衣服穿着吧你，30的白板拿着把你） 经过了以上种种，在路上走得好好的，突然来俩大怪巡逻卡死角直接走你背后，先手打你5下直接把你2个人物打死，爽的一比 然后呢，死出来重开跟上局一样，一点局外成长加成没有，继续随机吧你就 离谱

问题非常大，首先宣发的时候说有局外成长，然而仅仅能给你解锁新技能，成长数值完全锁死，你以为解锁新技能就有用吗？戳啦！最多也只会给你一些辣鸡技能，还需要你用10点解锁，10点啥概念？大概率能换来3点属性，而且你一共也就42点，失心疯了才去换个下到3层可能都要被迫遗忘的技能。如果你对DRPG有一定了解，那么你一般都可以稳扎稳打混过前2层，即使队友不那么给力，也可以通过合理规划AP整个勉强能用的队出来。然而到了第3层，你的对手直接从苍蝇/鱼这种小卡拉米升级成魔像，差距有多大呢？第3层的小怪弱的接不下你一发质子炮（无弱点暴击500-600），强如魔像可以吃你三发不死，你以为这就完了？第三层BOSS一个物免法师一个魔免战士一个辅助回血样样精通的奶妈，你200多血的角色接一个二连就死，打不死BOSS连数值都没得看，哦抱歉打死了也不一定有的看，打死一次开图鉴，打死两次看等级，三次以上才能看HP等数据，像极了为了结个婚彩礼五金订婚婚礼关关难过关关过的江西老表

Its a fast and short game, but oh boy. When I say "Imagine Etrian Odyssey 1" I mean imagine the worst parts of that game like the boss fights and mechanics. Colonoscopies are a common around these parts, nothing to ease it either.
Haven't played much yet, but so far my first impressions are that this is everything you could want from a roguelike (not roguelite).

很难说那些推荐这游戏的是不是赤石后抱着祸害其它人的想法的… 以下涉及内容剧透 玩了4个小时体验下来给我的感觉就是游戏内容过于的匮乏，所以制作者故意设了一个难度跨度极大的屎设来拖游戏时长 地图只有4层，每层会有好几个不同的迷宫，前两层难度偏低，第一层是新手教学用于熟悉操作和流程，第二层开始难度略微提升，小怪需要一定的队伍配合或者全员菜刀才能做到无伤一回合杀（所谓的OTK），第三层开始难度骤升，小怪血量提升到了近千血甚至就是千血以上，这个时候我就感觉到不对劲了，于是在第三层几个迷宫里泡了一段时间用于升级 到四层，难度在第三层的基础上翻了1.5~3倍，怪血普遍两千血到五千血之间，幸亏第三层练了菜刀，无脑用终极技打，无限之光+炼狱+虚无+犹大，直伤在400~900之间，虽然没办法一回合杀，但凭借之前积累的道具和尽可能在两回合内击杀做到减耗倒也能扛得住损伤 第四层结尾要打游戏的关底BOSS，假如在这层，玩家没有探索周围，没有把那几个柱子封印全部解除的话，打的会十分艰难（解除好像会出现收割者，类似小BOSS，血量在5000左右），BOSS血可能有几十万？打了N轮看着BOSS又是全能力下降又是死亡宣言，又是召唤小弟，又是全体特效炫酷的技能，又是自己回血，又是挨个点名即死，属于是拼尽全力无法战胜了 把柱子清掉后BOSS血大概在8000~10000这之间，如果有练极的话其实还挺好打的，三到五回合灌伤灌死BOSS 游戏最强法术不知道是不是无限之光，其它法术不上BUFF和给怪上DEBUFF的情况下也就打个600~800，无限之光能灌出1000~1300的直伤本身还是全体的范围法术 然后如果能行的话弄一个领域也好直接学队友的也好，穿刺者（无视敌人的法术抗性）被动会十分舒服 局外成长几乎为0，值得换的技能只有两个被动，对法术直接增伤的秘法火花（增加15%法术伤害）和直接增加生存的求生本能（闪避几率提升15%）其余的要么是下到三层要被遗忘改成学习队友的技能要么是对伤害或是生存而言提升过小，亦或是用来领悟新技能的基底技能 最终结论，说这游戏是DRPG不如说是套着DRPG皮粗制滥造的刷子游戏，不刷级想过就是不可能，治疗意义为0，全队菜刀想办法赶快杀死怪物远比常规双坦单C单奶或是单坦大C辅C单奶玩起来更轻松 物理是蛆中蛆（怪又硬血又厚物理手还短靠近就要被怪白嫖打一轮），物毒是蛆（毒伤害不是百分比伤害而是持续直伤，还不吃属性加成，二十多级毒还是十位数伤害，完全意义不明），元素法爷是神（根据怪的克制打元素伤害很公式化，搭配元素DEBUFF轻松打出爆炸伤害），驱魔是神上神（谁能懂光系法术开局就能秒秒秒的救赎感，后面怪开始有光抗就玩暗系法术也能打出克制伤害打超高爆发，终极技无限之光更是神上神） 击败最终BOSS后也没有什么可看的，只有几个红色的万花筒（阿玛特拉斯）图形搭配几段话，大致意思就是你们成功肘出冥界活了很棒，可以自由决定生死了，然后就是单局时长步数记录……（便宜制作的手游既视感拉满）

Booted the game up and was hooked immediately, I got pretty far in on my first run, completely shredded on my second run and wound up demolishing the game on my third run. If you want the short and sweet of it, it's a roguelike (not roguelite!) dungeon crawler that has quite a lot of variety to it. It blends the feeling of old school dungeon crawlers including an actual combat toggle (you can enter or leave combat at the cost of a full party-wide turn), as well as a hint of a horror game through its impeccable atmosphere. My first run felt like I was playing a horror game at times and it hooked me in with that. You'll probably wipe several times while you're getting your bearings but if you've any experience with the genre as well as a bit of luck, it's quite lenient for your first clear. TLDR; I hate reducing it to this but think something like Darkest Dungeon meets Wizardry and Etrian Odyssey combined. After your first run, you'll have the option to add modifiers to your run and either start with a randomly generated character, or create your own. There are options for adding your own custom portraits, as well as naming the character yourself (though it appears that the character naming is a bit bugged out at the time of writing this review unfortunately!). You'll be given a number of points to work with, and you can spend them however you see fit with either more powerful starting equipment, additional skills, or higher base stats. Classes can also be rerolled and have 7 skills each by default, but you are also able to either develop new skills from your older ones, or learn skills from party members, as well as even learning their class. The latter option won't always give you the same abilities as that party member either, so you can get quite a bit of variety with your party compositions considering there are a lot of classes. The actual combat is what you may expect from a blobber. You select an action between attacking, waiting, guarding, using items or using various skills and continue at it until either your party or the enemies are defeated. What is different is that a character being knocked out isn't necessarily enough to kill somebody off. Each time you're knocked out, you accumulate a wound, which increases the chances of that party member dying the next time they're knocked out. One of the modifiers you can unlock also includes the option to add stat penalties to the character when this occurs, but more on that later. Wounds do slowly fade away though, so it's not quite as punishing as it seems. The atmosphere of the game deserves some serious praise. Every single area feels distinct and uniquely terrifying as you're going through it the first time. Enemy types may also change between runs, as I noticed some monsters showing up that I hadn't seen before. It can definitely be a bit of a fright to turn the corner into an intimidating looking monster, especially when you're already playing cautiously and checking your corners. The music blends creepy ambient noises with fittingly intense combat music as you swap between being actively in combat and exploring. The boss theme definitely deserves special praise as getting me right on edge, and the rest music is incredibly calming. You probably won't be humming these tunes, but they're excellent at creating the overall mood the game has. While I have a good idea as to what's going on with the story, I feel there are a lot more secrets to uncover, so I'll definitely be aiming for at least another couple clears. I touched on it lightly before, but the game provides you with the option to modify your runs. This could be something as simple as having all enemies be several levels higher, to making it so wounds have various stat penalties as mentioned earlier, to taking more damage overall, and so on and so forth. There's even one that disables your auto-mapping feature and the dev definitely was being cheeky with it considering the description. There are a few bugs I did notice, such as my controls resetting upon restarting the game for my controller, but the mouse and keyboard seemed to remain as it was with no issues. The menuing can be a little cumbersome as well, but once you get used to it, it isn't too bad. With another layer of polish in removing bugs like enemies casting group-wide buffs making them display on your party members (purely visual, you don't also get buffed), or certain ranges feeling a bit off for certain relics, the game will truly shine. For the current price, the game is a steal and I'd highly recommend it to anybody interested in dungeon crawlers or roguelikes. I could just be woefully uninformed, but it's rare to find an actual honest-to-god roguelike in this day and age where most people conflate or mistake the term to apply to roguelites with meta progression. The only thing you keep between runs here is knowledge and the ability to make your runs more difficult as you clear it, so there's definitely some good replay value to be had here if you're worried about it being too short.

Thysaistery is, at first glance, a very striking game. Its gloomy visual palette and oppressive darkness give the dungeon crawler a powerful atmosphere. The sound design reinforces this mood beautifully, creating a sense of dread and tension as you explore. The game also introduces an interesting cross–party skill teaching system, allowing party members to learn abilities from each other, which is a genuinely creative mechanic. Unfortunately, after the initial hours, the game begins to fall short of its potential. The biggest problem is the combat system. Calling it flawed would be generous. Combat revolves almost entirely around exploiting enemy weaknesses and landing critical hits to stagger enemies and push their actions further down the turn order. In theory this is a good idea. In practice it creates a miserable experience. Enemies hit dramatically harder than the player. Mages can be one-shot, and even front-line fighters can be killed in two hits. The defensive options are extremely limited. There is a basic miss chance, but there are no meaningful defensive systems such as deflection, counterattacks, or reliable damage mitigation for melee characters. There is a reflect spell, but because hero skills are learned randomly, you may or may not even have access to it when you actually need it. Damage balance is also heavily skewed. Regular enemies often require multiple party members working together just to kill a single target. If you fail to finish them quickly, they retaliate with devastating damage. Spells can deal strong damage, but even they often require two or three casts to finish an enemy. The result is that most encounters require your entire party focusing down a single foe while hoping you do not take lethal damage in return. Group fights are even worse. Some enemies can hit the entire party while applying debuffs like bleeding, which can reduce everyone to one hit point. That situation alone can wipe a run if you do not immediately recover. Resource management adds another layer of frustration. The main character can learn a skill called Cauterize, which removes wounds but deals significant damage to the user. Wounds themselves are essentially stacking penalties to your death saves. On top of that, the game does not restore health or TP (the equivalent of MP) after a certain number of steps outside of combat. Every dungeon floor becomes an endurance test where you are slowly ground down. Boss fights make the issue even worse. Despite the game being a largely linear challenge gauntlet, bosses frequently spawn additional enemies during the fight. This turns encounters into pure damage-per-turn checks rather than strategic battles. It feels similar to the classic Resident Evil ammo problem: you spend the entire game carefully conserving resources only to have a boss fight demand that you expend nearly everything just to survive. In the end, the combat becomes a slog. The game’s art direction, atmosphere, and creative ideas show real promise, but the balance issues and punishing combat design overshadow those strengths. What could have been a memorable dungeon crawler instead becomes a frustrating endurance test.

Awfully balanced. No understanding of dungeon crawlers and very little understanding of roguelikes on display from the dev team here. I don't even know where to start... The immediate thing that comes to mind is just how bad the classes and party build feel from a basic level. The classes have trees but the trees are randomized, and thus you can end up with a fighter that's a good fighter and a fighter that's barely able to output physical damage or take a hit. This is made worse by armour value and the front/back row system being barely useful compared to the average dungeon crawler. In a game like Wizardry acquiring a better piece of armour for your frontline fighters was IMMEDIATELY reflected when you're taking 0-2 damage, but this was offset by the fact that fighters were limited by their attack range and consistent but unimpressive damage output. On the flipside your casters usually start off so weak they almost feel like a waste in your party, but as they grow in power and obtain a larger pool of mana they would become key to large damage output and crowd control. None of this has been considered when putting these classes together; instead the dev has opted to make classes work like something from a roguelite JRPG. More armour just means your frontline fighters take 1/4 of their total hp per hit rather than 1/3rd now and this is problematic when you rely on RNG for item drops. I've done about 4 runs now and each one just ended because an enemy decided it would no longer receive hits, move out of range, kill a character during a free move when I am forced to exit and re-enter combat to move into range, and I am mathematically unable to win the encounter due to damage output vs healing resources/output or any other tools to curb the disparity. Seriously if you're a fan of dungeon crawlers this games blatantly display of misunderstanding is going to infuriate you. If you like roguelikes then I hope you also like gambling because the balance is entirely around RNG, not knowledge and planning.

个人从几年前的《世界树的迷宫123重制版》后就再也没有接触过DRPG类型作品，简单来说DRPG就是以第一人称+地牢/迷宫探索为核心，采用回合制、格子移动等玩法的迷宫探索游戏，而《祭祀地宫》正是一款风格令人眼前一亮的复古像素风DRPG，游戏在画面加持下的地宫氛围也塑造十分不错，只不过游戏好玩是好玩，但难也是真的难。 [h2] 经典框架下的探索与成长 [/h2] DRPG的核心魅力在于探索与成长，在漆黑无比的地牢中每一步都可能是未知的，玩家可能会在探索时前往一些没有任何奖励的死胡同，也有可能“转角遇见爱”或是经过已探索的地方突然出现怪物的袭击等等，同时地牢不单单只有敌人，也有各种可互动内容，宝箱、商人、祭坛、石碑、壁画、各种神秘事件等等，丰富了玩家的探索体验。 而成长方面，玩家会在探索时累计经验提升等级，从而用获得的AP值来学习技能或从基础技能中领悟全新技能，也可在达到一定等级后消耗AP提升基础属性，虽然本作没有局外成长内容，但由于人物职业丰富，技能数量足足有270个，在地牢内学习全新技能后都可在下局开始前从自定义角色中进行属性加点、携带已学习的技能或各种装备，但强度高的依然是那几个技能，其它算是锦上添花。 [h2] 精妙的“心神凝聚”，不平衡的难度曲线 [/h2] 随着等级越高越强力的技能所消耗的MP也会增多，并且基于游戏数值问题，从第三关开始难度骤然上升（被两套攻击团灭的痛苦谁懂啊），而游戏里设计了“心神凝聚”机制，玩家可通过不断移动会使人物集中精神，在此状态下人物技能不仅会被增强，技能所消耗的MP也会大幅降低，这常常会使一个非常强力的技能也就消耗个位数MP，从而形成了与敌人绕圈拉扯的跑打玩法（近战在本作中仅在前两层有用），一般可与击退敌人或延缓敌人行动的技能搭配起来使用，但由于是地牢玩家无法在可视拐角处或是没有地板的区域攻击敌人，所以游戏除技能不同效果、数值、距离外也就没什么太大区别了，此外不同敌人也有不同特性和差异性，面对相克属性攻击会造成更多伤害，但面对同属性攻击则会免疫伤害，这一点也要在每次战斗时要思考一下。 整体体验下来，游戏因为要移动走格子、还要频繁转视角等等，在长时间游玩下来还是会有些疲惫感的，其次，获得物品仅会有ERROR：Bad format的提示，翻译方面也存在一定问题。 [h2] 总结 [/h2] 《祭祀地宫》作为DRPG在初体验还是给到我不少惊喜，它用复古像素美学和扎实的氛围吸引着玩家，独特的“心神凝聚”机制也有着有趣的体验，但游戏重复可玩性并不高，虽有肉鸽元素但在关卡构建上没什么太大体现，核心驱动力还是在于尝试不同的职业和技能组合，一旦拿到强力技能稍微练练级即使在第三四关也可以差不多平推了，总体来说作为一款独立游戏确实值得尝试，但也希望制作组能平滑一下关卡体验。 [quote]漫话漫谈，期待关注:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44551694/]写生漫话家[/url] ←节约宝贵时间，阅读省流测评~ 欢迎加入漫话家的大家庭:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/14030826]写生漫话家[/url]←共同探讨游戏中的精彩片段，向玩家展现第九艺术的魅力~

A gear-dependent dungeon crawler where you're reliant on random gear drops and all commerce is done via one-for-one randomized trading with a NPC that randomly spawns. A party-based Rogue-Like where your party's small skill pools are cross-class and randomly assigned. So much of the game is randomized that the few control points stick out like a sore thumb and actually damage the replay value for me. The game either needs a class rework, the ability to start with a full party, or more ways to recruit party members. As it is now though the game is just too frustrating to recommend because of poor randomization decisions. There's three main class archetypes that all of the unique classes fall under: Fighter, Mage, and Healer. The problems start with how skills are randomly assigned on character generation: characters receive a pool of passives and actives of half of one archetype and half of another. Sometimes this works, like STR/INT "mage blade" builds, and sometimes it's useless garbage, like a so-called Healer that has one actual healing skill and the rest are front line melee attacks (but with a Healer's stats). You have a little control over this with custom character creation at game start, but this only affects your first party member. This much harsh randomization doesn't make sense even within the game's systems because you can gain access to other character's skill pools with multi-classing. Even if you think you have a decent party, you'll need a full suite of multiple ranged attacks, various elemental attacks to exploit weaknesses, multiple heals, and multiple cleanses to even have a chance at beating the game. The third dungeon boss feels like a MMO raid boss, and enemies in the fourth dungeon love dumping multiple debilitating status ailments on your party every turn too. Combat can be clunky and frustrating because later enemies often have ranged attacks that can hit you outside of combat, there's no "wait" command outside of combat, and no movement while in combat (even though enemies can stay engaged away from you). Thysiastery feels like so many other indie games I've played and haven't reviewed in the past year: like a game dev jam project expanded out with a budget. It has wonderful aesthetics, good monster and skill variety, but has randomization in the wrong places. With some fixes it could be decent but I'd rather see some systems completely reworked and new systems added... At that point you might as well make a sequel though. The game is fine (if you don't plan on beating it) but I can't recommend it, especially given how many other dungeon crawlers and traditional Rogue-Likes do this better.

Thysiastery is one of the best games I have played in years. I will be purchasing any and all expansions or sequels, forever. The combination of elements—ambience, sound, music, gameplay (focus on combat, item discovery, and exploration... with no puzzles, thank God), 90s-style party-based adventure, dark fantasy theme—is near-perfect. I could play this endlessly and only wish it was more expansive. Contemporary gamers often don't understand how today's typically hyper-realistic games can reduce the mental experience on the part of the player. The games of the 90s, by contrast, with primitive graphics and less-realistic looking worlds, actually allowed the imagination to play a larger role in drawing you into a fantasy experience co-created by your own thoughts and feelings. Thysiastery does an amazing job of returning to an early style and genre of party-based dungeon crawlers. (To see where this kind of game comes from, look at Ancients 1: Death Watch [1991] and Ancients II: Approaching Evil [1994].) The whining babies writing negative reviews about the gameplay "lacking balance" and being too hard simply do not understand this game. It's supposed to require many attempts before achieving success. The degree of challenge is by design, and I'm so glad that it took repeated attempts to finish rather than being the once-through-and-done kind of experience that apparently many players want. The game creates incentive for extended engagement because you have to learn how to maximize and exploit every minor advantage in order to reach the end of the game. Small decisions can have outsized consequences here, and it pays to play slowly and think about what you're doing. Set aside expectations and don't anticipate that the game will conform to what you're familiar with. It deserves to be experienced on its own terms. I heartily affirm that the experience is rewarding.

恶意满满。 复古的点阵图风格让游戏画面令人眼前一亮。游戏机制中唯二的亮点一是心神专注，处在该状态下伤害会大量提高，并且降低技能消耗，而难度很大程度上都与技能消耗强相关，因此心神相关的技能会十分的逆天。 二则是DRPG的迷宫行动机制，心神会在移动中回复，如果在与强敌的战斗中用完了心神，直接脱离战斗开始绕圈回复心神会是个不错的选择，但现阶段下玩家很难获得击退手段来避免脱战时被攻击，浪费了这个灵活脱离战斗的设计，如果有着更丰富的位移手段，那么这个系统可以玩出花。 众多的缺点：游戏的机制相当隐晦，数值看不到，UI操作也不知道结果，全要靠试，技能干脆不到解锁就不清楚效果。角色技能表是随机的，如果你的队友的技能搭配过于糟糕，那就很难走下去。不但技能随机，掉落也逆天般随机。技能学习成本太高，升3级才能学个1阶技能，2阶要7点，学习技能还要过（战斗推进）时间，如果不清图甚至刷图，到boss前都很难有趁手的技能用。没有复活！！！ ROUGE+DRPG的组合也许让本作拥有以丰富的配置组合挑战高难地牢的玩点，但RPG刷子的本质与高难机制下的重试成本产生的矛盾，让它显得恶意满满。

Generally speaking, dungeon crawlers fall into two categories: ones that put emphasis on world building, usually with a bit of story to spice things up, and ones that put emphasis on combat. These two paths aren't mutually exclusive, indeed some of my fondest memories are associated with the "Might & Magic" series, particularly parts 4 through 7, which attempted to strike a balance. "Thysiastery" leans decidedly in favour of the combat. Here's why it doesn't quite work out: - There isn't much depth to the mechanics. Your goal is simply to optimise your resource expenditure vs. progress. Enemies respawn, so you're generally better off *not* exploring, let alone backtracking to the camp. Small detours make sense if you spot a chest or a shrine, but other than that you just keep looking for the exit and hope you find it before the monsters overwhelm you. - Enemies hit hard, meaning that it's difficult to plan ahead, because one or two unlucky rolls already send your characters to the grave. There's very little you can do to stop or prevent this, because you can't plan ahead due to lack of information. On one run, you might find four sets of (not particularly useful) armour. On another, there's going to be ammunition for a gun you don't have instead. - There's no such thing as a combo here. Enemies come with basic weaknesses and resistances, and keeping these in mind will give you an advantage, but that's basically a matter of persistence (kill enough enemies to learn their weaknesses) and memorization. - The random dungeon generator yields nondescript, amorphous spaces without structure. Some small parts are actually hand-crafted, and these work much better! This game would probably work better overall as a classic top-down roguelike where such things don't matter because you can see the entire board at a glance. But instead of this it uses a (fairly restricted) first-person view, and the result is you just stumble from one intersection to another, since they all look alike. The aesthetic choice, while pleasing to the eye, definitely didn't help here. Everything is monochrome and shrouded in shadow, so it looks even more samey. - Since everything is random and anonymous, there's nothing to focus your attention on. For instance, levelling up doesn't matter because characters are randomly generated, die quickly, then get replaced at the nearest camp. Gear doesn't matter, because it's always the same random junk. Environments don't matter because they look like nothing in particular. I could go on. - All of the above combined also means there's no pacing. Steam says I haven't even played for three hours, but I could swear each level just kept going on and on and on.

Thysiastery is a rogue-like Wizardry inspired corridor rpg where you explore a brutal maze set under a WW1-like battlefield with a handful of individuals trying to escape the trap. The plot is mysterious and esoteric, but there's a lot of style and implied lore. However, the real meat and bones is the gameplay. Thysiastery is very difficult, but it does the rogue-like better than most titles, with the beginnings feeling fresh due to a high variance of player classes, recruits you find, and equipment options. Many rogues have a very samey beginning and it can be a chore. The first areas of Thysia go fast once you learn the game and it becomes a lot of fun to see what options are presented for you to adapt to. The sheer amount of powers, which you can learn and teach to your other companions, is very large and most of them are useful once you know what to do with them. Classes have a distinct feel and the subclasses for each are also numerous. You'll never play the same composition twice. For those who want more control, you also have the option to customize your first character with a point buy system and the options are both generous and balanced. Thysiastery does not hold your hand. You will die. A LOT. Once your gone, you're gone, but while total party death ends your session and you don't start with improved gear as in some other rogues, this one works with you using your mind as you flesh out the monsters list, which in time eventually allows you to see their statistics. Thanks to a system not terribly dissimilar to Persona combat, you need to target enemy weaknesses to an edge. Thus knowing what to use when, in which the monster list gets more details as you beat them over several runs, is what will really benefit you. Powerleveling is less a thing here. While you can grind a little bit, you need to keep moving. Each dungeon floor has an invisible timer based on your total turns and time spent resting or studying steles for ability points. Take too long and a crazy brutal enemy called a Harvester will chase you until you leave. In most cases, it's certain death to stay and fight one, but running isn't impossible. The art is very unique, I'm not sure what I could compare it to- pay no mind to the generic fantasy cover art on the Store page, the in game depictions of monsters and mercs are detailed, distinctive, and moody, much like the unsettling musical score. While I see the occasional bug with the random gen mazes not allowing all paths to be accessible or chests being stuck in walls, it's usually not too bad. However, one design aspect sticks in my craw a bit and those of others from what I've read. You have to be mindful of your positioning and distance from the enemy before a combat begins, as they'll get a shot on you in many cases as you approach if not with surprise. You need to lure them behind a corner usually to get around this or just ambush, which is common to do. But because of this movement/attack interaction, enemies can annoying move away during combat, whereas you have to exit combat to pursue them instead of just moving forward while in combat mode. This feels clunky and unnecessary. That said, that's my only gripe and it doesn't come up that often. I absolutely love this game and it's my current GOTY. With the sheer variety available and each run really feeling unique alongside an exotic strange horror adventure in a tough but satisfying rpg like this, I highly recommend Thysiastery and hope to see more content from this hidden gem of a game.

A definite recommend. I haven't been this engaged with a new game for quite a while. I initially thought the balance was questionable, but that is only the newbie phase. Once you learn the ins and outs of the game, the balance is actually quite good overall. Pros: -Game attempts to step outside of the generic fantasy enemies. There are some very unique designs. -The weakness system works really well. In most games it is a system kind of ignored, but here there is a lot of incentive to try and find and exploit weaknesses on enemies. -The roguelike random elements are also done well. For example, it is beneficial to have a healer, but any class can get access to heals so you aren't locked into a very specific set of classes every run. I had a run where my healer was a high dex vampire ninja. Cons: -The skill system is unintuitive and messy. Chances are you'll beat the game before you understand all the aspects of it. None of the skills have numbers attached to them, so it is a bit of a guessing game of what a skill is doing. -If you aren't interested in repeated runs with or without difficulty modifiers (think climbing ascensions in Slay the Spire) then the game is short-ish. You'll probably faceplant a few times, but chances are you'll "beat" the game in 10-20 hours depending on success rates. However, if you do like repeated runs, there is potential a ton of hours here.

[h3]A fantastic old-school techno-occult dungeon crawler where a group of misfits brave the horrors of the labyrinth in a brutal struggle for survival.[/h3] I have always had a soft spot for the more traditional style dungeon crawlers such as Eye of the Beholder, Lands of Lore or lately Legend of Grimrock, and Thysiastery takes that concept and really boils it down to a smooth minimalistic package oozing with atmosphere. In Thysiastery you begin the journey as a solitary survivor breaking out of a decrepit prison filled with undead amalgamations from the last war. On your explorations you build up your party, claim loot and defeat monsters and miscreants on your way to escape the labyrinth's stratified halls. The variation of classes, skills and items are plentiful, and should you choose you can of course make your own character at the start of the run, all with their own quirks and specialities. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3741428704 The game takes place traversing a selection of floors on your way to freedom where each floor of the labyrinth takes on a different biome with different types of enemies. To properly defeat your foes you have to mix up your abilities so that you always have an answer to the next gribbly horror storming down the passageway to end your run in a mess of entrails and bloody tears. To combat this peculiar problem you have plenty of unique skills and abilities to master, and since the game's standard mode is a random character at start you never really know what toolbox you will begin the game with. The game also has a rather interesting teaching/learning system that lets your Timelost Magi to learn Femur Breaker, or your Backstreet Thug Blessing of Light, the sky is the limit when it comes to tailoring your rag-tag band of gritty survivors. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3741428355 When it comes to the atmosphere, the monochrome colours and the bleak presentation really do some heavy lifting. Each biome feels unique in its oppressive otherness and you have to constantly consider your movement, lest a terrible foe catches up with you to end your path of freedom. The graphics are really suited to this kind of game and truly encapsulates a world steeped in botanical occultism and techno-sorcery. Personally I really adore this Obra Dinn like minimalism, but it might not be for everyone. The monsters you encounter as well as the bosses you have to defeat come from a great selection of fantastical, mundane and technological sources and somehow work in the grander scheme of things. The worldbuilding is sublime, yet always lingering in the background with tons of lore waiting to be exhumed. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3741429016 [b]Conclusion:[/b] All in all, Thysiastery is a great example of the old dungeon crawling concept given a slightly modern take. As you delve more and more you unlock more and more skills and learn more about the various creatures and their stats and weaknesses giving you a slight edge during your coming run. I highly recommend this game to anyone interested in a great yet slightly simplistic dungeon exploring RPG. There is a roadmap on the storepage and the developers are active in the forums so I suspect I will return to the labyrinth plenty of times in the coming seasons. [h1]你能逃脱成为祭品的命运吗？复古像素风的地牢逃亡之旅 [/h1] [h2]前言—— [/h2] 没有人知道这座迷宫从哪里来，也没有人知道这座迷宫真正的出口在哪里。唯一可以明确得知的是——这座迷宫正在饥渴地吞噬着所有进入其中的人，而每个在迷宫里的冒险者，都将成为迷宫的祭品！ [h2]游戏介绍—— [/h2] 《祭祀地宫》是一款由芬兰制作团队DIRGA开发的复古像素风rpg肉鸽地牢游戏，游戏开场每个人控制的都是一群被神秘力量召唤进入迷宫的【烙印之人】。 我们需要去探索并试图逃离这座迷宫，随着探索的深入，途中会遇到危机四伏的森林、沉没的城市遗迹、奇怪的科技造物，以及遇到各种愿意加入的队友。 而让人感到后背发凉的是，所有进入者也许根本不是被召唤来的探险家、冒险者，而只是一个个献给迷宫的血肉祭品。 [h2] 第一人称视角移动机制——[/h2] 如果是曾经玩过其他硬核地牢rpg的牢玩家，那么看到祭祀地宫里的视角设计一定不会陌生。玩家在迷宫中一格一格移动，通过Q和E来左右转动视角，触发事件、遭遇敌人、开启宝箱，。 第一人称的视角，加上网格式的移动方式，每次转身也许就是未知的敌人或者宝箱，让人感觉仿佛自己就深处迷宫之中。 [h2] 回合制的战斗设计——[/h2] 游戏中可以随时进入战斗状态，无论面前有没有出现敌人。 如果真的遇到了敌人，进入战斗状态后就是按照回合进行轮流行动，使用技能、攻击、道具来击败敌人，或者是趁敌人还没发现你抢先从旁边埋伏一手。 网格距离也是战斗力很重要的一点，每个攻击手段都有范围距离，一旦超出就没法命中，只能往前移动拉近距离后再尝试攻击。 [h2]跨职业的技能传授—— [/h2] 不想做奶妈的战士不是好法师，游戏里对于职业的限制并不严格，我们可以让队友之间互相传授职业自己的技能，让法师学会治疗，让战士学会法术。 和常规的固定职业rpg游戏不同，队伍的职业构筑在这个游戏里变得非常自由，通过不同的技能搭配可以建立起一支玩家理想的队伍。 [h2] 角色的心神凝聚——[/h2] 越强力的技能，需要消耗的法力值MP也会越多，尤其是面对强敌需要用强力技能终结却发现没有法力那就糟糕了。 游戏里的战斗设计有一个特殊机制，那就是心神凝聚，玩家通过不断的移动可以使得队员们进入心神凝聚状态，在此状态下人物释放技能需要的MP会变得很少，效果也会变强。 这就延伸出了放风筝战术，通过移动和拐角来遮蔽敌人视线，自己给角色上心神凝聚buff后释放强力技能来决战。 [quote]欢迎关注鉴赏家：[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/DCYXJLB] 大川游戏俱乐部 [/url] 欢迎加入Steam组：[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45300930] 大川游戏俱乐部 [/url]来一起感受游戏的乐趣 喜欢这篇评论，也可以顺手点个赞哟[/quote]

7.5/10 The blobber genre has always been a bit on the shallow side. Core elements like plot, depth, or even heavy strategy usually aren’t the main focus, and Thsiastery sticks pretty close to that formula. That said, I genuinely enjoyed my time with it. It took me about 11 hours and 8 attempts to finally complete a run, which felt like a good balance of challenge without overstaying its welcome. The skill system is easily the standout feature. Skills are randomized, but the ability for party members to train each other at any time adds a layer of flexibility that kept things interesting throughout. While the game is light on storytelling, the atmosphere really carries it. It has this bleak, somber tone that almost feels like Berserk at the end of the world; dark, oppressive, and strangely captivating. Overall, I appreciated that Thsiastery knew what it wanted to be. It delivers a focused experience and doesn’t try to stretch itself into a 100+ hour commitment. A short, enjoyable run that I’m glad I picked up.

I really wanted to like this game. It has great art and a fantastic atmosphere... but I've never played a dungeon crawler that wants you to explore less. Enemies hit like a truck after the intro level (I ran into a slime monster that almost wiped my party in seconds almost immediately after entering the first level) and they constantly respawn while you have very limited resources, meaning you're dying by a thousand cuts if you want to actually look around. And when I say constantly, I mean in a matter of minutes. Not just when your party rests. You can't escape enemies either. Once they lock onto you, you either fight them or they slowly punch you to death from behind, dealing a good 1/3 or more of your life every hit. Your characters have randomized skills that come with their class and they can teach those skills to other people, which is a neat idea but this often leads to having a lot of useless skills. Learning skills is expensive and skill points aren't exactly plentiful and even worse, learning skills takes time, which it often feels you don't have thanks to the respawning enemies constantly bleeding you out. I was left wishing this was more of a standard dungeon crawler with a bit more lore, a bit less randomization and a bit less of a focus on brutalizing the player.
